proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), fix the least-sampled cell \(g_\star\), and put
\[
\Theta(P)=\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\tau_1(P).
\]
All constants below may depend on the fixed center and its strict interior margins.  By thm:nested-derivative, the derivative of \(\Theta\) in cell \(g_\star\) is the sum of (i) a leading outer Green functional, whose Riesz representer is \(\varphi_{g_\star}\), and (ii) the second elliptic and harmonic functionals, whose Riesz representers have bounded \(L^2(P_{0g_\star})\) norm.

Let \(x_\star\) be the unique preimage, in the \(g_\star\)-cell coordinates, of the outer pole \(y_1\).  It is unique because \(R_0\) and \(T\) are diffeomorphisms.  Freeze \(B\) at \(y_1\).  Direct substitution into \(-\operatorname{div}(B(y_1)\nabla G)=\delta_{y_1}\) shows that its two-dimensional fundamental solution is
\[
G_0(y_1,z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B(y_1)}}
 \log\left|B(y_1)^{-1/2}(z-y_1)\right|.
\tag{1}
\]
Subtracting a smooth cutoff of \(G_0\) from the periodic Green solution leaves an equation whose right-hand side is locally bounded: indeed
\[
-\operatorname{div}\{B(z)\nabla(G-G_0)(z)\}
=\operatorname{div}\{(B(z)-B(y_1))\nabla G_0(z)\}+b(z),
\tag{2}
\]
where \(b\) is bounded near the pole, and \(B(z)-B(y_1)=O(|z-y_1|)\).  Since \(\nabla G_0=O(|z-y_1|^{-1})\), the vector field on the right of (2) is bounded.  Integrating (2) on dyadic annuli and rescaling each annulus to unit size gives, for every integer \(0\leq m\leq s\),
\[
\left|\nabla^m\!\left(\nabla_{y_1}G(y_1,z)-\nabla_{y_1}G_0(y_1,z)\right)\right|
\leq C_{P_0}|z-y_1|^{-m}\{1+|\log|z-y_1||\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The pullbacks in def:nested-derivative are \(C^{s-1}\) diffeomorphisms with nonsingular Jacobians.  Consequently (1)--(3), after the appropriate pullback, give
\[
\varphi_{g_\star}(x)
=\frac{b_{g_\star}^{\mathsf T}(x-x_\star)}
 {|E_{g_\star}(x-x_\star)|^2}+r_{g_\star}(x),
\qquad b_{g_\star}\neq0,
\tag{4}
\]
on a fixed ball about \(x_\star\), where \(E_{g_\star}\) is invertible and the derivatives of \(r_{g_\star}\) satisfy the bounds inherited from (3).  The vector \(b_{g_\star}\) is nonzero because \(\upsilon\neq0\), every coordinate pullback has full rank, \(B(y_1)\) is positive definite, and the cell multiplier is either \(1\) or \(\alpha(y_1)>0\).  This explicitly uses density positivity and inner and outer ellipticity.

Polar integration in (4) now yields constants \(a_{g_\star}(P_0)>0\) and \(C_{P_0}<\infty\) such that
\[
\int \chi_\varepsilon^2\varphi_{g_\star}^2\,dP_{0g_\star}
=a_{g_\star}(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon)+O_{P_0}(1).
\tag{5}
\]
The centering integral \(\int\chi_\varepsilon\varphi_{g_\star},dP_{0g_\star}\) is bounded, because \(|x-x_\star|^{-1}\) is locally integrable in two dimensions.  Thus subtracting it changes the squared norm in (5) by only \(O_{P_0}(1)\).  This proves the asserted two-sided logarithmic norm bounds after decreasing the admissible upper bound for \(\varepsilon\).  Leibniz's rule, (3)--(4), and the defining transition bounds for \(\chi_\varepsilon\) give
\[
\max_{0\leq m\leq s}\lVert\nabla^m(\chi_\varepsilon\varphi_{g_\star})\rVert_\infty
\leq C_{P_0}\varepsilon^{-s-1}.
\tag{6}
\]
Centering adds a constant, and multiplication by the fixed \(C^s\) density \(f_{0g_\star}\) preserves (6).  This is the claimed \(C^s\) envelope.

Put
\[
u_n=\frac{\zeta\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}}
 {\sqrt n\,\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}}.
\tag{7}
\]
By construction \(\int u_n\,dP_{0g_\star}=0\), so both perturbed densities have mass one.  Equations (5)--(6) imply
\[
\lVert u_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}=\frac{\zeta}{\sqrt n},
\qquad
\lVert f_{0g_\star}u_n\rVert_{C^s}
\leq
\frac{C_{P_0}\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-s-1}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}}=o(1),
\tag{8}
\]
because \(\varepsilon_n=n^{-\eta}\) and \(\eta(s+1)<1/2\).  The same display with \(s=0\) shows \(\lVert u_n\rVert_\infty=o(1)\).  Hence \(1\pm u_n>0\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Since \(P_0\) is an interior point relative to the \(C^s\) topology, (8) places both alternatives in \(\mathcal F_s\) once the sample threshold is chosen using the fixed center's positivity, ellipticity, lift, and cut-locus margins.

For completeness, this membership has the advertised causal representation.  For either alternative let \(p=\operatorname{OT}(P_{C0},P_{C1})\) and \(T=\operatorname{OT}(P_{T1},p\#P_{T0})\), and set
\[
h_0=\operatorname{id},\quad \nu_C=P_{C0},\quad \nu_T=P_{T0},
\quad h_1=p,\quad h_{1\star}=T^{-1}\circ p.
\tag{9}
\]
Then \(h_1\#\nu_C=P_{C1}\) and
\[
h_{1\star}\#\nu_T
=T^{-1}\#(p\#P_{T0})=P_{T1}.
\tag{10}
\]
Moreover \(h_1\circ h_0^{-1}=p\) and \(h_1\circ h_{1\star}^{-1}=T\), so both required graphs are \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone by their defining optimality.  The fixed-center interior argument following (8) supplies the needed diffeomorphism, ellipticity, branch, and cut-locus conditions; none of these conditions sets a harmonic translation equal to zero.

Using \((\sqrt{1+v}-1)^2\leq v^2\) for \(|v|\leq1/2\), (7) gives
\[
\operatorname{Hel}^2(P_{n,\pm,g_\star},P_{0g_\star})
\leq\int u_n^2\,dP_{0g_\star}=\frac{\zeta^2}{n}.
\tag{11}
\]
All other cells are unchanged, proving membership in \(\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa)\) when \(C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\kappa\).  Similarly,
\[
\operatorname{Hel}^2(P_{n,+,g_\star},P_{n,-,g_\star})
\leq C\int u_n^2\,dP_{0g_\star}\leq C\frac{\zeta^2}{n}.
\tag{12}
\]
The elementary product inequality \(\operatorname{Hel}^2(\otimes_iQ_i,\otimes_iR_i)\leq\sum_i\operatorname{Hel}^2(Q_i,R_i)\), together with \(n_{g_\star}=n\), turns (12) into the asserted product-experiment bound.  Choosing \(\zeta_0(P_0)\) smaller if necessary makes it at most \(1/2\).

It remains to verify separation, including the selected translations.  Center \(\varphi_{g_\star}\) without changing its action on mean-zero scores.  From the definition of \(\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\), (4), and local integrability outside the retained annulus,
\[
\int\varphi_{g_\star}\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\,dP_{0g_\star}
=\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_2^2+O_{P_0}(1).
\tag{13}
\]
The bounded \(L^2\) representers of the second elliptic and harmonic pieces contribute only \(O_{P_0}(\zeta n^{-1/2})\) when paired with (7).  Thus thm:nested-derivative and (13) give
\[
D\Theta_{P_0}[f_{0g_\star}u_n]
=\frac{\zeta}{\sqrt n}\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_2
+O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{14}
\]

We finally control the deterministic local remainder without invoking the unresolved uniform shrinking-bandwidth assertion.  Along the segment \(P(t)\), \(-1\leq t\leq1\), having changed-cell density \(f_{0g_\star}(1+t u_n)\), subtract the two linearized inner and outer elliptic equations at \(P(t)\) and \(P_0\).  Their coefficient differences are bounded by \(C_{P_0}\lVert f_{0g_\star}u_n\rVert_{C^s}\).  The resolvent identity
\[
\mathcal L_{B_t}^{-1}-\mathcal L_{B_0}^{-1}
=\mathcal L_{B_t}^{-1}(\mathcal L_{B_0}-\mathcal L_{B_t})\mathcal L_{B_0}^{-1}
\tag{15}
\]
and its inner analogue, tested on the fixed annulus supporting \(u_n\), give
\[
\sup_{|t|\leq1}|x_\star(P(t))-x_\star(P_0)|
\leq C_{P_0}\lVert u_n\rVert_2\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}
=O_{P_0,\zeta}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}n}\right)
=o(\varepsilon_n).
\tag{16}
\]
The last equality uses \(\eta<1/[2(s+1)]<1/2\).  On each dyadic annulus the coefficient part of (15) has \(L^2\) norm at most \(C_{P_0}\lVert f_{0g_\star}u_n\rVert_{C^s}\), times the constant frozen-pole mass on that annulus.  There are \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon_n))\) annuli.  Translating a pole by \(d_n^{\mathrm{pole}}\) changes the gradient kernel on the truncated region by at most \(C_{P_0}d_n^{\mathrm{pole}}/\varepsilon_n\) in \(L^2\), by the mean-value theorem and the \(|x-x_\star|^{-2}\) derivative of the leading term in (4).  Cauchy--Schwarz therefore yields
\[
\left|(D\Theta_{P(t)}-D\Theta_{P_0})[f_{0g_\star}u_n]\right|
\leq C_{P_0}\lVert u_n\rVert_2
\left\{
 \lVert f_{0g_\star}u_n\rVert_{C^s}
 \sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}
+\frac{d_n^{\mathrm{pole}}}{\varepsilon_n}
\right\}.
\tag{17}
\]
Here \(d_n^{\mathrm{pole}}\) denotes the left side of (16).  All non-Green and harmonic terms have bounded \(L^2\) kernels and satisfy (17) without either singular factor.

Integrating (17) over \(t\in[-1,1]\), and using (8) and (16), bounds the remainder in the two-sided difference by
\[
C_{P_0,\zeta}\frac{\varepsilon_n^{-s-1}}{n}
+C_{P_0,\zeta}\frac{\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}}{n\varepsilon_n}
=o\!\left(\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}{n}}\right),
\tag{18}
\]
because \(n^{-1/2}\varepsilon_n^{-s-1}/\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}\to0\) and \(n^{-1/2}\varepsilon_n^{-1}\to0\).  Equations (5), (14), and (18) therefore imply
\[
|\Theta(P_{n,+})-\Theta(P_{n,-})|
\geq c_1(P_0)\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}{n}}
\tag{19}
\]
for a smaller positive \(c_1(P_0)\).

For the harmonic translations themselves, thm:nested-derivative states that the maps from a cellwise density score to \(\dot a_p\) and \(\dot a_T\) have uniformly bounded \(L^2\) Riesz scores.  Along \(P(t)\), positivity from (8) makes the \(L^2(P(t))\) and \(L^2(P_0)\) norms equivalent.  Hence (7) and the fundamental theorem of calculus give, for either sign,
\[
\lVert a_p(P_{n,\pm})-a_p(P_0)\rVert
+\lVert a_T(P_{n,\pm})-a_T(P_0)\rVert
\leq C_{P_0}\int_0^1\lVert u_n\rVert_{L^2(P_0)}\,dt
=O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{20}
\]
Since \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=\eta\log n\to\infty\), (20) is little-oh of the scale in (19).  This proves every part of the fixed-center statement.

Suppose that \(f_g\equiv1\) for all four cells.  The identity coupling has zero cost from the uniform law to itself, while \(c_{\mathbb T}\geq0\); uniqueness of the optimal map therefore gives
\[
p=T=R_0=\operatorname{id},\qquad S=H=D=I_2,qquad \alpha=1,qquad A=B=\mathsf C=I_2.
\tag{20}
\]
Because \(\nabla\alpha=0\), the second elliptic term in def:nested-derivative is zero.  At the identity map a lifted first variation has the Hodge form \(v=a+\nabla u\), with \(u\) periodic and mean zero.  The linearized pushforward equation fixes \(-\Delta u\) and does not involve \(a\).  The second-order transport cost is
\[
\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^2}|a+\nabla u|^2
=\frac12|a|^2+\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^2}|\nabla u|^2,
\tag{21}
\]
because \(\int_{\mathbb T^2}\nabla u=0\).  Optimality thus forces \(a=0\).  Applying this argument to the inner and outer variations gives \(\dot a_p=\dot a_T=0\), so \(\mathcal H_P=0\).  Substitution into def:nested-derivative yields exactly
\[
\mathcal D_P[\delta]
=\nabla(-\Delta)^{-1}(-\delta_{C0}+\delta_{C1}+\delta_{T0}-\delta_{T1}).
\tag{22}
\]

Let \(\widehat K_2(\xi)=\widehat K(\xi_1)\widehat K(\xi_2)\).  For one cell, Parseval's identity applied to (22) gives the pointwise covariance
\[
Q_h=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}}
\frac{mm^{\mathsf T}}{4\pi^2|m|^4}|\widehat K_2(hm)|^2.
\tag{23}
\]
Symmetry makes the off-diagonal entries zero and the diagonal entries equal.  Since \(\widehat K_2(0)=1\), its smoothness gives \(\widehat K_2(hm)=1+O((h|m|)^2)\) for \(|m|\leq h^{-1}\), while compact support and smoothness of \(K\) give rapid Fourier decay beyond that range.  Comparing the lattice sum with polar annuli and using
\[
\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}\,d\omega=\pi I_2
\tag{24}
\]
therefore yields
\[
Q_h=\frac{I_2}{4\pi}\log(1/h)+O(1).
\tag{25}
\]
The four samples are independent, so their covariances add and the four signs in (22) disappear after squaring.  If their limiting size ratios all equal one, division by \(\log(1/h)\) gives \(V_j=4I_2/(4\pi)=I_2/\pi\).  If the source is fixed and only \(P_{T1}\) is sampled, only the last term of (22) remains and the covariance is \(I_2/(4\pi)\), as asserted.

The displayed lifts have Jacobians
\[
Dh_0^{\mathrm{sep}}=I_2,qquad
Dh_1^{\mathrm{sep}}=\operatorname{diag}(1+0.2\cos(2\pi u_1),1),
\tag{26}
\]
\[
Dh_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}
=\operatorname{diag}(1+0.3\cos(2\pi u_1),1-0.1\cos(2\pi u_2)).
\tag{27}
\]
Their eigenvalues lie in \([1,1]\), \([0.8,1.2]\), and \([0.7,1.3]\), respectively.  Thus they are orientation-preserving periodic diffeomorphisms.  They are gradients of strictly convex equivariant Euclidean lifts, and their periodic potentials, obtained by direct differentiation and normalized to have mean zero, are
\[
\phi_{h_1}(u)=-\frac{0.1}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_1),
\qquad
\phi_{h_{1\star}}(u)=-\frac{0.15}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_1)
+\frac{0.05}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_2).
\tag{28}
\]
The displacement averages of \(h_0^{\mathrm{sep}}\), \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}\) are zero, so their selected translation coordinates are zero.

Both latent laws are uniform and \(h_0^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the identity.  Hence lem:torus-cic-identification gives
\[
p=h_1^{\mathrm{sep}},qquad
T=h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\circ(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}})^{-1}.
\tag{29}
\]
At \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\), the chain rule and (26)--(27) give
\[
H(y)=\operatorname{diag}\left(
\frac{1+0.2\cos(2\pi u_1)}{1+0.3\cos(2\pi u_1)},
\frac{1}{1-0.1\cos(2\pi u_2)}
\right).
\tag{30}
\]
The eigenvalue ranges are \([12/13,8/7]\) and \([10/11,10/9]\), so \(H\) is uniformly positive definite.  Change of variables gives
\[
\frac56\leq f_{C1}\leq\frac54,
\qquad
\frac{100}{143}\leq f_{T1}\leq\frac{100}{63},
\tag{31}
\]
while \(f_{C0}=f_{T0}=1\).  All four densities are smooth.  Thus the density, smoothness, and ellipticity requirements hold whenever the class constants contain the explicit bounds in (26)--(31).

The two compositions required by ass:cic-identification are \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(T\).  Their lifted Jacobians are symmetric and positive definite by (26) and (30), hence their lifts are gradients of strictly convex functions.  Their coordinate displacements are bounded respectively by \(0.1/\pi\) and \(0.05/\pi\), strictly below \(1/2\).  Convex duality on each such unambiguous squared-distance branch gives the torus transport dual inequality with equality on the graph; summing this inequality over a cycle proves \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclical monotonicity.  The selected translations of \(p\) and \(T\) are zero.  For \(T\), this can also be checked directly by changing variables \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\): each component of \(T(y)-y\) is a sine multiplied by a product of constants and cosines, and hence has zero integral.  The distance of both translations from the boundary of \(\mathcal Q\) is \(1/2\), and the graph distances from the cut locus are positive because the preceding displacement bounds are strict.  Choosing \(\beta\) below these margins proves ass:lift-regularity and therefore \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\in\mathcal F_s\).

At \(u=(1/4,1/4)\), all cosines in (30) vanish and
\[
y-T(y)=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)-h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)
=\left(\frac{0.05}{\pi},-\frac{0.05}{\pi}\right)\neq0.
\tag{32}
\]
At the same point \(H(y)=I_2\), \(f_{T1}(y)=1\), and \(\alpha(y)=1\).  With equal cell-size ratios, the definition of \(V(P)\) gives \(w_j=4\) and hence
\[
V_j=\frac{4I_2}{4\pi}=\frac{I_2}{\pi}.
\tag{33}
\]
This proves the claimed nonzero causal displacement and covariance check.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are positive constants \(c_1(P_0),c_2(P_0),C_{P_0},\zeta_0(P_0)\) and a sample threshold, all allowed to depend on the \(C^s\), ellipticity, lift-branch, and cut-locus margins of \(P_0\), such that, for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\),
\[
c_1(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon)
\leq \lVert\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}^2
\leq c_2(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon),
\qquad
\lVert f_{0g_\star}\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_{C^s}
\leq C_{P_0}\varepsilon^{-s-1}.
\]
For every fixed \(0<\zeta\leq\zeta_0(P_0)\) satisfying \(C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\kappa\), the laws in def:green-local-alternatives satisfy, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
P_{n,+},P_{n,-}\in\mathcal F_s\cap\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa),
\]
\[
\operatorname{Hel}^2\!\left(
\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,+,g}^{\otimes n_g},
\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,-,g}^{\otimes n_g}
\right)
\leq C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\frac12,
\]
and
\[
\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|
\geq c_1(P_0)\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}{n}}.
\]
Here \(\eta<1/[2(s+1)]\) makes the \(C^s\) perturbation tend to zero.  For either sign, causal-class membership is witnessed by \(h_0=\operatorname{id}\), \(\nu_C=P_{n,\pm,C0}\), \(\nu_T=P_{n,\pm,T0}\), \(h_1=p\), and \(h_{1\star}=T^{-1}\circ p\).  Moreover,
\[
\lVert a_p(P_{n,\pm})-a_p(P_0)\rVert
+\lVert a_T(P_{n,\pm})-a_T(P_0)\rVert=O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
so the selected-lift harmonic changes are negligible relative to \(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)/n}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim incorrectly asks for constants uniform over all interior centers, although relative interior gives only a center-specific distance to the density, ellipticity, lift-branch, and cut-locus boundaries. The proposed fixed-center claim retains the explicit alternatives, product-Hellinger bound, Green separation, and harmonic-translation conclusion required by the directive.

For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are a class-wide constant \(C_1>0\) and center-dependent constants \(c_0(P_0)>0\) and \(\kappa(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\leq C_1\frac{L_n}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{n}{L_n}
\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
\mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\geq c_0(P_0).
\]
The lower bound is witnessed by def:green-local-alternatives and lem:green-local-alternatives, for which \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\).  The upper bound remains the uniform assertion over \(\mathcal F_s\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The Green alternatives are valid at each fixed interior center with constants and a threshold depending on that center's margins. Accordingly the local lower-bound radius and constant must be written as \(\kappa(P_0)\) and \(c_0(P_0)\); the class-uniform upper-risk assertion is left unchanged.

proposed.justification: The lemma audits the fixed-center converse through a named annular Green tangent, normalized alternatives, class membership, bounded product-experiment distance, quantitative estimand separation, and an explicit bound for both selected harmonic translations.
proposed.gap: Single-scale global-map perturbations do not accumulate the pointwise logarithm. This fixed-center construction does so while keeping its cutoff independent of the estimator bandwidth; its constants legitimately depend on the center's interior margins.

\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\leq C_1\frac{L_n}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[

proposed.justification: The fixed-center Green two-point experiment proves that the logarithmic lower scale is information-theoretic. Matching still requires the unresolved uniform moment upper bound for the plug-in estimator.
proposed.gap: Existing global one-map lower bounds do not give the pointwise logarithm or the nested four-cell experiment. The lower bound is now fixed-center and explicit; the class-uniform upper bound remains tied to uniform critical control.
proposed.consumer: Once the upper moment bound closes, the theorem will distinguish information-limited uncertainty from a smoothing artifact in the Card--Krueger arrow analysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Propagate the fixed-center dependence of the local experiment to the theorem's lower-bound constants while preserving the class-uniform upper-risk assertion as an open part of the same target.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniformly prove the transformed-kernel variable-coefficient Green covariance and \(o(\sqrt{L_n})\) score stability under estimated coefficients and moving poles, together with the \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\) nonlinear nested remainder.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fixed-center annular resolvent bound does not control a bandwidth-scale random pole displacement. Pointwise coefficient consistency is insufficient because a pole error comparable to \(h_n\) changes the singular score at leading order. The frozen results provide the exact derivative and bandwidth arithmetic but not this uniform stochastic stability or the required mixed tame estimate.
open_obligations.attempted: The coefficient was frozen at a deterministic pole, the anisotropic fundamental solution was subtracted on dyadic annuli, and the uniform-law Fourier case was evaluated. These close the deterministic fixed-center lower-bound construction and the constant-coefficient check, but they do not justify replacing full transformed KDE scores by frozen-pole scores.
open_obligations.partial_result:
At a fixed center and a deterministic annular tangent, freezing \(B\) at a fixed pole gives the anisotropic logarithmic fundamental solution
\[
-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}\log|B(y)^{-1/2}(z-y)|,
\]
whose gradient has squared mass proportional to \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).  The proof of lem:green-local-alternatives controls this fixed-center response and its selected translations.  The uniform-law Fourier calculation in prop:uniform-reduction also gives the exact constant \(I_2/(4\pi)\) per sampled cell.  These facts do not control a data-dependent transformed KDE, estimated coefficient, or moving pole uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Upgrade the algebraic four-cell frozen-pole covariance to operator-norm convergence of the exact full score covariance, uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The second elliptic and harmonic pieces are bounded, but the leading transformed-KDE response still needs the unresolved uniform coefficient, generated-target, and moving-pole stability from oeq:uniform-critical-control.
open_obligations.attempted: The cellwise mass identities, local intensities, anisotropic angular constant, independence across cells, and absence of off-grid logarithmic cross terms were derived explicitly.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The mass-change identities at a pole \(y\), with \(x=R_0(y)\), are
\[
f_{C0}(x)\det D(y)=f_{C1}(T(y))\det H(y)=\frac{f_{T1}(y)}{\alpha(y)},
\]
\[
f_{T0}(x)\det D(y)=f_{T1}(y).
\]
Thus multiplication by the leading control weight \(\alpha(y)\) gives local noise intensity \(\alpha(y)f_{T1}(y)\) for each control cell, while each treated cell has intensity \(f_{T1}(y)\).  A frozen coefficient \(B(y)\) maps intensity \(q_y\) to the logarithmic covariance
\[
\frac{q_y B(y)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}.
\]
Since \(B=f_{T1}H^{-1}\), summing independent cells gives algebraically
\[
\frac{\bigl[\alpha(y)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})+
ho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\bigr]
\sqrt{\det H(y)}H(y)}{4\pi f_{T1}(y)}.
\]
Distinct fixed grid points have distinct pulled-back poles, so their cross blocks have no logarithmic term.  What remains unproved is that the full variable-coefficient, transformed-KDE score differs from these frozen-pole responses by \(o(\sqrt{L_n})\) in \(L^2\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Show that the nonlinear plug-in estimator is uniformly asymptotically equivalent to its oracle triangular-array linear score.
open_obligations.obstruction: The oracle Lindeberg calculation and deterministic bias arithmetic close, but neither implies the moving-pole score replacement nor the uniform quadratic nested remainder. Those are precisely the unresolved parts of oeq:uniform-critical-control.
open_obligations.attempted: The oracle summand envelope was compared with the normalization, and the bandwidth window was checked to imply Lindeberg negligibility; the available fixed-center argument cannot be promoted to a uniform random-pole expansion.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For the oracle linear term
\[
S_n=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i}),
\]
the smoothed Green envelope is \(O(h_n^{-1})\).  Hence every summand of \(\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\) is
\[
O\!\left((n h_n^2L_n)^{-1/2}\right)=o(1),
\]
and the independent triangular-array Lindeberg condition follows because \(a_h<1/9<1/2\).  Conditional on the unresolved covariance convergence, this proves the Gaussian limit for the oracle linear term.  Lem:bandwidth-feasibility makes the order-minus-two bias negligible.  The missing steps are the uniform oracle-to-plug-in score replacement and the nonlinear nested remainder \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove normalized \(L^2\) consistency of every cross-fitted adjoint score when coefficients, coordinate pullbacks, harmonic scores, and evaluation poles are estimated.
open_obligations.obstruction: Cross-fitting removes own-observation dependence but does not control the singular gradient score. A pilot pole error must be \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\), and the resulting translated transformed kernel must be stable by \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n})\) in score norm; neither bound follows from the frozen map-consistency statements.
open_obligations.attempted: Conditional on the pilots, the empirical covariance decomposition and exact multiplier covariance were computed. The missing singular-score stability was isolated rather than replaced by ordinary coefficient consistency.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Cross-fitting makes each evaluation-fold score conditionally independent of its pilot.  If the pilot adjoint score obeyed
\[
\max_{g,r}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n}),
\]
then conditional second-moment expansion and the empirical law of large numbers would give
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-\Sigma_{h_n}(P)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
Also, directly from the definitions and Gaussian multiplier independence,
\[
Z^\star\mid\{X_{g,i}\}\sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}).
\]
The unresolved point is the displayed score-stability bound, particularly for transformed kernels and an estimated pole; ordinary coefficient consistency does not imply it at the critical logarithmic scale.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Complete the asymptotic coverage proof after establishing the joint critical CLT and adjoint covariance consistency.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite-sample invertibility and the conditional Gaussian identity hold exactly, but coverage requires the two unresolved parent limits. Without them, quantile consistency cannot be asserted for the estimation error.
open_obligations.attempted: The finite-sample ridge argument, conditional multiplier law, limiting maximum distribution, and quantile-continuity step were derived conditional on the two parent convergence results.
open_obligations.partial_result:
In every sample \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\succeq0\) because it is a sum of outer products, and \(\theta_n=n^{-1}>0\), so
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^R=\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}+\theta_nI_{2J}\succ0.
\]
Every principal block is therefore invertible and the conditional quantile is finite and nonnegative.  Moreover
\[
Z^\star\mid\{X_{g,i}\}\sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}).
\]
If thm:joint-critical-clt and thm:adjoint-covariance are established, both the multiplier maximum and the studentized estimation-error maximum converge to
\[
M=\max_{1\leq j\leq J}Z_j^{\mathsf T}V_j^{-1}Z_j,
\qquad Z\sim N(0,V).
\]
Because \(V\) is block diagonal, \(M\) is the maximum of \(J\) independent \(\chi^2_2\) variables, with continuous distribution function \((1-e^{-x/2})^J\).  Quantile convergence then gives simultaneous coverage.  The two required parent convergence results remain open.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the class-uniform upper moment bound \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2\lesssim L_n/n\).
open_obligations.obstruction: A weak Gaussian limit would not by itself give the asserted risk bound. Uniform integrable tail control of the exceptional lift branch and the nonlinear nested remainder is still required and is part of the unresolved uniform critical-control problem.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-center lower bound was completed by the explicit Green alternatives and an elementary two-point testing reduction. The upper bound was separated from this completed converse rather than inferred from weak convergence.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The fixed-center lower bound is complete.  Write
\[
\Delta_n=\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|.
\]
For any estimator, the test choosing the nearer of the two scalar parameter values is wrong only where the scalar estimation error is at least \(\Delta_n/2\).  Therefore
\[
\max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}\mathbb E_{P_{n,\sigma}}
\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P_{n,\sigma})\rVert^2
\geq\frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}
\left(1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_{n,+},Q_{n,-})\right),
\]
where \(Q_{n,\sigma}=\bigotimes_gP_{n,\sigma,g}^{\otimes n_g}\).  The elementary inequality \(\operatorname{TV}(Q,R)\leq\operatorname{Hel}(Q,R)\) and lem:green-local-alternatives give a center-dependent positive lower bound for the parenthesis.  Since
\[
\Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}n,
\qquad
\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=\frac{\eta}{a_h}L_n,
\]
the asserted local minimax lower bound follows with \(c_0(P_0)>0\) and \(\kappa(P_0)>0\).  The class-uniform upper risk bound is not implied by weak convergence and still requires uniform integrable tail control for the unresolved nonlinear plug-in remainder.

prose_updates.tldr: The intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes identification and exact four-input derivative are established, including nonzero harmonic translation modes. This round proves the fixed-center Green-aligned product-Hellinger alternatives, their \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)/n\) separation, and the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) size of both selected-translation changes; it also verifies the uniform-law Fourier reduction and a smooth nonzero separable witness. The general-density critical Gaussian limit, full four-cell covariance convergence, adjoint consistency, simultaneous asymptotic coverage, and uniform upper risk remain conditional on one explicit analytic gap: transformed-KDE stability at an estimated moving pole plus the uniform nonlinear tame remainder.

project_justification.gap: Published transport central-limit results do not prove a pointwise gradient limit in dimension two for general variable coefficients with a generated target, and published global minimax bounds do not supply the nested four-cell pointwise logarithmic local experiment. The remaining gap is specifically uniform shrinking-bandwidth control of transformed kernels, estimated coefficients and poles, and the nested nonlinear remainder.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, a Green gradient has logarithmically divergent variance, while nesting makes each control sample enter both directly and through the generated target. Independent samples prevent cancellation. The fixed-center converse can be proved without resolving the harder uniform random-pole expansion.
project_justification.fill: The note establishes intrinsic torus identification, a translation-aware lift, the exact nested derivative, bandwidth feasibility, fixed-center annular Green alternatives with explicit harmonic-translation control, a uniform-law Fourier benchmark, and a smooth nonzero separable benchmark. It records the candidate four-cell covariance and adjoint ellipse procedure, but labels their general-density asymptotic validity as open until the transformed-KDE moving-pole and nonlinear tame estimates are proved.

prose_updates.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC motivates cyclic-comonotone changes-in-changes and the Card--Krueger application but does not prove the intrinsic torus identification used here. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT supplies periodized-KDE and Monge--Ampere tools and proves the uniform-law dimension-two special case, while leaving general variable coefficients open. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supports one smooth density-path linearization; the exact four-input generated-target derivative is established in this note. The 2026 Green-influence results identify pole singularities but do not supply the shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical limit, and GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT excludes pointwise gradients. HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin concern global one-map risk; the present fixed-center annular construction supplies a distinct pointwise logarithmic lower-bound mechanism. PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand motivates simultaneous transport uncertainty in one dimension, but the proposed bivariate ellipses still await singular-adjoint consistency.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved analytic module is uniform control of the variable-coefficient pole after transformed KDE smoothing. The required numerical kill test remains: on one nonseparable smooth torus law with nonconstant \(f_{T0}/f_{C0}\), compute cellwise adjoint covariance increments at \(h,h/2,h/4,h/8\), refine the PDE mesh until discretization changes are negligible, and separately track generated-target, harmonic, coefficient, and pole remainders. A slope discrepancy, a logarithmically divergent normalized remainder, or failure of \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) pole accuracy invalidates the proposed general-density inference spine. The fixed-center local lower bound does not resolve this random-pole problem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope consists of intrinsic torus causal identification, the exact nested derivative, bandwidth arithmetic, a fixed-center Hellinger-local logarithmic lower-bound construction whose constants \(c_0(P_0)\), \(\kappa(P_0)\), and sample threshold may depend on the center's interior margins, the uniform-law covariance reduction, and a nonzero smooth separable witness. No general-density critical CLT, adjoint covariance consistency, simultaneous asymptotic coverage, or class-uniform upper-risk theorem is claimed until oeq:uniform-critical-control is resolved. The ellipses are fixed-grid procedures, not confidence bands over the torus.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the first-class analytic bottleneck; fixed-center annular control is insufficient for random transformed kernels and moving estimated poles.
statement_notes.gap: A proof must deliver normalized score stability and the nonlinear tame remainder uniformly over the model class, rather than assuming them from map consistency.
statement_notes.consumer: Its resolution is required before the covariance, Gaussian limit, adjoint inference, ellipse coverage, and uniform upper-risk claims can close.

statement_notes.justification: At each fixed interior center, the annular Green tangent has logarithmic squared norm, stays inside the smooth causal class after normalization, and yields the claimed two-point separation while both selected translations move only at order \(n^{-1/2}\).
statement_notes.gap: The constants are center-dependent because relative interior supplies a center-specific margin; no uniformity over all interior centers is asserted.
statement_notes.consumer: This proves the local minimax lower-bound half of thm:matched-critical-risk.

statement_notes.justification: The fixed-center logarithmic lower bound is proved, with \(c_0(P_0)\) and \(\kappa(P_0)\) explicit as center-dependent constants.
statement_notes.gap: The class-uniform upper moment bound remains open because weak convergence does not provide uniform integrability or exceptional-branch tail control.
statement_notes.consumer: A matched rate certificate will become available only after the upper bound is established.
